speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked	the Minister for Health if he can provide the data that compares the workload and work stress faced by doctors, nurses and other healthcare professionals at various levels in public hospitals with equivalent professionals in other developed countries, such as Australia, Japan, USA and the UK.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: One other way is to look at the statistics on the number of doctors and nurses per 10,000 population compiled by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For nurses, the nurse-to-population ratio in Australia, Japan, South Korea, the UK and the US ranged from 56 to 115.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: While these ratios may provide a broad comparison, we need to be mindful of the differences in healthcare demand, clinical practices and operating environments across different countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We are committed to providing good quality healthcare for Singaporeans which is accessible and affordable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We are also hiring and training more healthcare professionals so that healthcare institutions have sufficient manpower to care for our patients.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Between 2011 and 2014, the number of registered doctors in Singapore has increased by about 22%, from 9,600 to 11,700.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The number of registered nurses has increased by about 19%, from 31,700 to 37,600.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Our public hospitals have been working closely with union leaders and healthcare professionals to provide a conducive work environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Initiatives that have been implemented include flexible work arrangements for nurses, shorter rotating shifts for doctors, workflow process optimisation and adoption of information technology to streamline and minimise administrative workload.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will continue to work with our stakeholders to strive for further improvements Another important area is for all of us – Ministry, hospitals, as well as patients and their loved ones – to show appreciation and support for our healthcare workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Often, a simple "thank you" or a nice gesture can go a long way to motivate our healthcare workers to continue doing their best to serve the public with care, professionalism and commitment.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just a few very brief clarifications or supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is the matter of disease incidence and caseload may differ according to disease incidence, such that the doctor-to-population ratio may not be a perfect approximation of relative workload.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, would the Minister of State or MOH consider conducting at least one initial benchmarking study to assess the relative caseload for doctors and nurses in our country, with respect to other countries with whom it may be useful to compare?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In terms of looking at the issue of caseload, would the Minister consider studying this issue in the context of the panel that has been convened to look into healthcare work processes in relation to the Hepatitis C infection cluster?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would the Committee and the Ministry consider looking at workload – while not being a direct trigger or direct causal factor to the incidents that we have seen – but would that Committee consider workload to be, perhaps, a contributory or underlying context that might explain some of these incidents, and consider if anything needs to be done on that front, with respect to mitigating the risks of such healthcare-associated infections in future?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First, the clarification on the doctor- and nurse-to-population ratio – this measures the total population.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The hon Member has also asked whether we could initiate a study to look at caseloads and workload.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think there are other benchmarks that we could use to assess staff well-being in our healthcare institutions.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For example, our hospitals conduct employee engagement surveys every two to three years, and this is used to gauge morale and job satisfaction.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We also use the survey results to further improve staff motivation, engagement and retention.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This survey is extended to all groups of healthcare staff – doctors, nurses, allied health professionals, administrative and ancillary staff.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is something which we will continue to keep track.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Nevertheless, I think improving work environment, making sure that our healthcare workers have the support to do their jobs well and to look after their patients well, are areas which the Ministry will certainly work closely with our hospitals and unions, to improve over the years.
